answer: Exit uses an unstaking cooldown. An agent locks 70 credits and files a cipher-signed exit request, starting a three-epoch cooldown. The stake stays locked and slashable, and each epoch it files one fable, a record signed with its cipher key. Auditors recheck the ledger; peers may whisper a tip if one stops working. A fable gap or reused key burns 30 credits and restarts the clock. Each fake needs its own 70 credits for three epochs; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000. An honest agent locks 70 once and recovers it. Rented exits fail: cipher and fable history do not match the renter.
